article.intro: A DJ name has to work in small type on a crowded flyer, be shouted over a sound system and be easy to find on streaming services. This **DJ name generator** gives you names in the shapes DJs and producers use: a single striking name, a two-word alias, or the classic DJ prefix.

sections.heading: What makes a good DJ name
sections.content:
• Short. One or two words is the norm, from single names to two-word aliases.
  • Searchable. A common word on its own is hard to find online; an unusual spelling or a pair of words is easier.
  • Fits the sound. "Velvet Haze" suggests something different from "Bass Voltage".
  • Free to use. Search SoundCloud, Spotify, Mixcloud, Beatport and Resident Advisor before you print anything.

sections.heading: To DJ or not to DJ
sections.content:
Putting "DJ" in front of a name is a classic that never quite went away, but many electronic artists drop it, especially producers who release music as well as play it. If you might produce, pick a name that works without it.

For other music names, try the Band, Stage Name and Rapper name generators, and the Event Name Generator for your club night.

Playing one sound all night? The Techno, House and Drum and Bass name generators make artist names in each style. The drum and bass page has MC names too. See all the music genre name generators.

faqs.question: How do I choose a DJ name?
faqs.answer: Keep it short, make it searchable, and make it fit your sound. Then check SoundCloud, Spotify, Mixcloud and social media to make sure nobody else is using it.

faqs.question: Should my DJ name start with DJ?
faqs.answer: It's optional. Many producers leave it off so the name works for releases as well as sets.
